What each one does, and what I did

The whole app: picker flow, preview pipeline, encoder retry loop, queue management, sharing, the settings screen and
No internet permission at all, so "offline" is enforced by the manifest rather than promised in copy. Preview encodes to
cache and deletes itself; nothing is written until you press compress.
Platform APIs only — no image library, no analytics, no SDK. The APK is under 300 KB because of it.
The fetch pipeline that pulls every free icon, recolours it to
, the filterable grid and the copy-to-clipboard
The icons are inlined in the page instead of fetched, so filtering is instant and the page still works with the network off
after load. Copy has a manual fallback because browsers refuse the clipboard on plain HTTP.
The same data is published as
, so the phone app will read exactly what the browser shows.
Static site · one palette · JSON catalogs
The measured layout, one shared stylesheet across seven pages, the JSON builder that re-measures every shipped
No framework and no build step for the pages — they are readable HTML. The build only generates what would
otherwise be retyped: the icon set and the catalogs.
Because the apps need the same facts the pages state. One catalog file feeds both, and the build fails if a page
The rules these were built under
If a feature needs the network, it either moves on-device or gets cut.
Nothing here asks you to sign in, and nothing collects anything about you.
The palette and spacing come from a Figma frame; the sizes on this site come from the files on disk.
